semantic_constraints.series: a business series is keyed by source, dataset, indicator, classification (NACE Rev.2 or a NAICS vintage), size class, place, adjustment (NSA, CA, SCA or not applicable), unit with its index base year and frequency; adjusted and unadjusted series, a rebased index and another NAICS vintage are always different series; values live in the Economics series storage (economic_vintages, dataset_observations)
semantic_constraints.vintages: each release that changes a series is an appended vintage with release and retrieval clocks (Eurostat LAST UPDATE, a declared CBP release date or the labelled retrieval time), revision_of and the recorded changes; a series a complete later release no longer states gets a removed_by_source vintage; as-of answers select the vintage released by the date and cite source, record revision and as-of time
semantic_constraints.flags: Eurostat OBS_FLAG letters and CBP noise flags and withheld markers are kept verbatim per value; a withheld, suppressed or confidential cell carries no value (never a zero) and is never reconstructed; a noise-infused value is never exact
semantic_constraints.definitions: each series cites its definition revision (statistical unit, scope, methodology notes, cited documents, CBP disclosure protection); a changed definition is a new revision
semantic_constraints.comparability: Eurostat enterprises and kind-of-activity units and Census establishments are different statistical units; answers list sources side by side with recorded differences, source-stated breaks, provisional periods and base-year changes; a pair without either is comparability_unknown; nothing is blended
semantic_constraints.identity: places match only through reviewed published codes; NACE and NAICS codes are linked only as reviewable candidate links through published concordances with their citations (relation exact, partial or one-to-many); nothing is merged or re-classified and unlinked codes stay queryable
semantic_constraints.links: links to economics.labour and economics.trade rest on a shared published code or accepted place matches, record the classification relation as evidence only and pin both revisions; absent providers and targets are reported, never dropped
semantic_constraints.minimisation: published aggregates only; person- and firm-level fields, business-register and survey microdata and single-business figures are never stored and are refused at write time
semantic_constraints.exclusions: no nowcasting, no filled periods, no re-based indices, no own seasonal adjustment, no blending of Eurostat and Census figures, no reconstruction of suppressed or noise-infused cells, no rates, shares or per-establishment figures of our own, no derived indicators, no forecasts
